title: Getting a helper to the right job
target: How to hand work to a helper in Supermarket Simulator without leaving a job half done: it covers the check the game runs first, the two errands a helper can be sent on, and the flags that say whether one is already busy.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: At least one helper on the payroll
Something that needs doing: a shelf to fill or goods to weigh
A till or a scale the helper can be sent to

steps.do: Check that the thing you want done can be handed over before you try to hand it over.
steps.because: the game keeps a kind of check of its own for whether something can be controlled by a helper (HelperControllableCheckType)

steps.do: Send the helper to the object that needs help when the job is about stock.
steps.because: there is a fetch for an object that needs help rather than a general instruction (FetchObjectNeedingHelp)

steps.do: Send the helper to the scale when the job is about weighing rather than fetching.
steps.because: the scale has its own fetch and its own start for helping (FetchScaleNeedingHelp, StartHelpScale)

steps.do: Use the checkout start for the till rather than the scale start.
steps.because: helping at the checkout and helping at the scale are separate instructions (StartHelpCheckout, StartHelpScale)

steps.do: Check whether the helper is already busy before assigning the next job.
steps.because: the game tracks being busy and being currently helpful as separate flags (IsCustomerHelperBusy, IsCustomerHelperHelping)

steps.do: Do not expect a helper to stand where you would: the game has a standing position for it.
steps.because: the helper is placed through standing and control transforms of its own (GetHelperControllableStandingTransform, GetHelperControllableControlTransform)

steps.do: Treat the helper as a configured kind rather than a person with preferences.
steps.because: a helper is described by its own data with an animation controller behind it (CustomerHelperSO, CustomerHelperAnimationController)

commonMistakes: Sending a helper to a job that cannot be controlled and wondering why nothing happens.
Assigning a second job while the busy flag is still set.
Using the scale instruction for a till, or the till instruction for weighing.
Standing where the helper is about to work and blocking it.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
